messages.author: Liam
messages.content_text:
June 18 Notes:


Today was one of the most frustrating trading days I have ever had in my life. This is going to be a long journal because of how many trades I missed and could have taken, but didn’t.
,
The overnight session rallied after tapping the nwog at the end of yesterdays session all the way until new york am session. Right off of 9:30 open we made an aggressive move down and we stopped and consolidated a little right above midnight open, which could have been the first bottom tick entry. It is a little scary cause it is close to market open, but the consolidation above the level is what gives it away. (Screenshot 1)
,
The next is the trade I took, we traded up into that 9:30 drop, tapped a 5min fvg and made a 5min rb out of it that we didn’t tap. We had a bunch of hourly lows stacked that made me thought we would be bearish so once 10:00 opened and traded into it. We got a 1min rb after tapping the 5min so I adjusted my stop to it and got stopped at the next candle. only $100 loss just cause I got the directional bias wrong. (Screenshot 2 & 3))
,
I was waiting for price to trade back down to 10:00 after we got the rally up, but once it finally did I hesitated setting my limit because there was only one candle lower. it was a 20pt wick so it was valid manipulation and everything else aligned too like the ote, el, so it was a great trade, but I faded it. (Screenshot 4)
,
I then also faded the 1min rejection block that happened after we tapped the 10:00 level. I faded it because it was a 1min bearish close followed by a bullish close, which is a valid rb, but I didn’t love the way it looked cause of the fast move down into 10:00. With this strategy I can’t be scared of fast moves down and that is hard. So another missed trade I could have taken. (Screenshot 5)
,

messages.content_text:
DAY 16  : 2 TRADES 2 L'S

TECHNICAL ANALYSIS
My bias today was bearish, from the unfilled NWOG and the unsweeped Daily low that we had today. Not to mention that we also hit a 4H FVG level on .62 discount. So it led me to believe that we wanted to go deliver down. From that 4HR FVG reaction, TFA aligned with 15 min, there was a 15 min OB TAP. TFA aligned with 1 min, i found a breaker leg, aligned it with OTE, and from there it was a good entry point. Price tapped me in. My stop was where the unmitigated swing high was, and did deliver down, but created equal lows and rejected off the OB and stopped me. Price closed above the .79 ratio so i closed early. Which was a good move since price ran through the high. 

From then, an SMT was created with ES being the heavier index. So i was looking to take shorts on ES. NQ reacted to a OB/RB and started moving down. ES reacted off of an OB. Level was tapped in discount. I looked for my breaker, and found it. I got tapped in, but after 10am KO was tapped and strongly reacted from it. I should have probably waited for a reaction and entry trigger from then instead of limiting. That probably was the only error that i could find aside from wrong bias.

Key takaways: BIAS, reacting off of NWOG at how big the gap is is probably stronger than a 4H gap. Bias was actually bullish today. 

PSYCHOLOGICAL ANALYSIS
I felt pretty good today. I executed flawlessly for once without hesitation and didn't take any risks that didn't align with my model or rules. Lost less than i could've so that was good too. It was just a wrong bias. Simple mistake, we can always get better at that discretion. No tilt, no revenge. We still have an account. We good. I am bummed that we didn't get any win this week. Next week is always a new opportunity. But at least the margin of error has been decreasing recently. (edited)

messages.content_text:
30 Day Challenge Recap

Overall, this was by far the most productive and eye-opening month of trading I've had. Not because it was perfect, but because for the first time I feel like I genuinely started becoming the trader I've always wanted to be.

The Good:


Multiple payouts and funded accounts earned.
,
Consistent journaling before, during, and after sessions.
,
More winning days than losing days.
,
Better patience and trade selection.
,
Started grading days based on execution and discipline rather than P&L.
,
Successfully locked myself out many times after hitting goals.
,
Significantly reduced the size and duration of spirals.
,
Began catching emotional mistakes in real time instead of after the damage was already done.
,
Built confidence in my actual strategy and market reads.
,

The Bad:


Still had moments of anticipation, FOMO, and forcing trades.
,
Blew a live account after running it up significantly.
,
Had a few F days caused by greed, revenge, and abandoning the original plan.
,
Continued to struggle at times with wanting more after already accomplishing the objective.
,
Success remains a larger threat than failure.
,

What Improved:
The biggest improvement was awareness. I can now recognize when I am becoming emotional, impatient, greedy, overconfident, or looking for action. In the past, I would realize this after the account was damaged. Now I often recognize it while it is happening and can stop myself before things get out of control.

My discipline also improved dramatically. Not perfect, but better than it has ever been. Locking accounts, accepting no-trade days, walking away after green, and focusing on process instead of money all became much more common.

What Needs Work:
Execution still needs improvement. Many losing trades were not caused by poor analysis but by entering too early, anticipating moves, or trying to force entries before confirmation.

june 17 Notes:


Today was fomc and despite looking for a trade during, I did not manage to find any. My tape read of the session was good, and I think tomorrow will be a good day if it continues to play out.
,
I did not trade am session because of the fomc in the afternoon, but 10:00 almost gave a nice setup, but missed by 2pts. 9:30 opened lower taking out london session lows and when 10:00 opened, the first 1min candle was a bullish rb. 11pt wick, may be considerable, but if you faded it would be smart because the low got swept and created a 5min rb with the first 10:00 candle. That would have 100% been a valid entry, but it edged by 2pts. Even if you took a loss on the 1min and tried again with the 5min that would have been a valid trading day. (Screenshot 1 & 2)
,
FOMC initial statement created a strong move down and market tapped the top of the nwog and made a 5min rb. We then did the classic FOMC amd model and traded back to the data high during the FOMC meeting (post 2:30) and we swept the data high and traded even lower, tapping the nwog ce creating the lotd. I wanted to enter at the sweep of the data high, but couldn’t really find a valid entry trigger. There was a 1min cisd, but it was too scary for me personally. I also wanted to enter longs, but we edged that initial rb out of the nwog and I wanted to see that tapped before moving higher. There were a couple of trades I saw during this fomc period, but market was moving with so much volatility, I got intimidated and faded everything. (Screenshot 3)

DAY 15  : 4 Trades 4 L

Technical Analysis
Bias was bullish after a 15 min RB was tapped. The overall bias is NWOG but i suspect that we will go higher to discount before reaching back down. Though this profile was not an ideal profile to trade. Seek and destroy profiles make for confusion and I got caught within it. I waited for the 1 min breaker to get invalidated and entered a limit as price closed above it. Perhaps the biggest mistake would have been that it was outside of the trading window. It's evident that after 8:30 that the volatility starts to die and consolidation begins. Problem found. 

Second trade was an early stoppage, but was honestly a mistake, i was using ote of the new leg to justify cutting the trade early. the trade delivered enough to break even but i cut the trade early. Bad risk management. 

Third trade was an early breaker tap entry, honestly entered in premium and had the chance to BE but didn't, that was a BE chance too. It was tapping an orderblock in discount short range, honestly should've BE'd there.

Fourth trade was a 15 min RB reaction to 1m breaker tap. Problem was that it was in premium and not discount.

3/4 trades i took had the right idea, but stopped me out. Entering in premium was a key mistake. Not properly managing risk was the second. Biggest thing was my DOL was not clear.

Psychological Analysis
Was certainly tilted. And it's clear that i broke my rules today. I didn't lose more than i would usually risk, but that shouldn't justify my actions. Second trade clearly tilted me, and was trying to get back or get some experience with FOMC. Man did that destroy me. 3rd trade i should have broke even watching it play out. I even debated it. 4th trade was the nail in the coffin. I even had the urge to go again, but by then my mental bandwidth was done for. I knew that i would just keep losing the more i traded. For one the PA was not in my favor, and two i was starting to make less and less clear decisions. I could have left today just down 100 but it resulted in -250. Confidence in model is weaker now. ,
I would skip this day regardless, but I think there was an interesting sequence. the 5min 10:00 candle technically made a 5min rb. It didn’t tap any pd arrays, you would just take this cause of the ballistically bullish market. That would be the first problem (no pd arrays) but if you look at the 1min time frame, the 10:00 candle made a 1min rb that also got used. This completely tarnishes the 5min rb that I saw people take. (Screenshot 1 & 2)
,
That is all for this day, never good in my books when we see that sort of extension off of pre market, or the size of opening gap.
